newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open slightly higher.

text.p: French stocks opened higher on Tuesday, buoyed by firmness in the dollar and bonds, brokers said.
But they said trading would be cautious ahead of the Federal Reserve Open Market Committee meeting beginning on Tuesday and U.S. leading indicators for December due out at 1500 GMT.
Bourse highlights included companies reshuffling holdings in media groups Havas and Canal Plus.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 7.94 points, or 0.32 percent, at 2,516.49 at 0940 GMT after opening at 2,514.44. The February CAC-40 futures contract was up four points at 2,520.
Volume was one billion francs in the first half hour.
Carmaker PSA Peugeot Citroen was the biggest loser on the CAC index, shedding 1.21 percent to 572 francs, after showing a huge drop in car sales in France in January.
Its car sales fell 43 percent in a market that shrank 33.6 percent from January 1996 levels. The company said it resisted joining in promotions until mid-month.

Shares in electrical engineering group Alcatel Alsthom were down 1.11 percent at 536 francs. Traders said investment firm Morgan Stanley placed 1.2 million Alcatel shares at 536 francs. Alcatel was not immediately available for comment.
The seller's identity was not known, but traders speculated it might be U.S. company ITT or insurer Axa.
Shares in Generale des Eaux rose 2.09 percent to 734 francs, extending their 1.55 percent gain on Monday. The group is seen as a prime beneficiary of an audiovisual industry restructuring.

Generale des Eaux and Havas confirmed on Monday they were in talks concerning their audiovisual activities, primarily Canal Plus. Newspapers said the operations under discussion would make Havas the biggest shareholder in Canal Plus and Generale des Eaux the key shareholder in Havas.

The Figaro said on Tuesday that bank Societe Generale also planned to swap its stake in Canal Plus for a larger share in Havas. Societe Generale declined comment. Its shares were down 0.47 percent at 636 francs.
Canal Plus shares were up 0.25 percent at 1,180 francs and Havas shares climbed 0.71 percent to 420 francs.
